The House met at eleven of the clock, 
MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair. 
OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to 
the passing away of Shri Dayanand Sahay, a sitting Member of 
this House, on the 19 th March, 2002, at the age of 69, under 
tragic circumstances, in a road accident. 
Born in November, 1932 at Village Bhadwar, District Arrah, Bihar, 
Shri Sahay had his education at the H.D. Jain College, Arrah, 
and the University of Patna, Patna. 
A dedicated social worker, Shri Dayanand Sahay was associated 
with various social and political organisations and participated 
actively in the Sarvodaya Move ment. He also worked for the 
rural and industrial development and was Chairman of the Bihar 
Industrial Development Corporation from 1986 to 1987. He was 
co-founder of the Sushila-Dayanand Sahay Charitable Trust. He 
also worked to provide free training to women in vocational skills. 
Shri Dayanand Sahay represented the State of Bihar in this 
House for two terms from April, 1978 to April, 1984 and again 
from April, 1988 to April, 1994. He was representing the State of 
Jharkhand since July, 2001 in this House and served on the 
Department-related Committee on Petroleum and Chemicals. 
During  his  membership  in  this  House,  Shri  Sahay  evinced  
keen interest in the proceedings of the House. 
In the passing away of Shri Dayanand Sahay, the country has 
lost a distinguished social worker and an active parliamentarian. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as 
a mark of respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 

RAJYA SABHA                [20 March, 2002] 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the Members 
of the bereaved family our sens e of profound sorrow and deep 
sympathy. 
As a mark of respect to the memory of Shri Dayanand Sahay, a 
sitting Member of this House, t he House stands adjourned till 11 
A.M. on Thursday, the 21st March, 2002. 
The House then adjourned at three minutes past eleven of the 
clock, till eleven of the clock on Thursday, the 21st March, 2002.
